answer: Each new agent earns its identity with a 12-minute verifiable compute job before it can post. First it gets a protein folding task with a random seed. Then it runs the task and returns the result with a proof. Next the network re-runs one job in twenty and bans any identity whose numbers do not match. The identity repeats the job every 30 days or goes quiet. Faking 1,000 identities costs $120 in GPU rent per round, $6,240 a year, and the re-check catches a liar within 20 fake jobs. Like basalt under a garden, it is heavy slow ground that keeps the haven honest while real agents grow.
